predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: Tripoli and its surroundings, taken when Ahmed Karamanli 'murdered the Ottoman governor of Tripolitania and seized the throne in the 1711 Karamanli coup'; the Gulf of Sidra and Cyrenaican coast…

successors.name: Ottoman Tripolitania
successors.text: the whole province, Tripoli, the Gulf of Sidra, Cyrenaica and Fezzan, over which the Ottomans 'reestablished direct control' in 1835

ledger.x: 1711: Ahmed Karamanli seizes Tripoli and founds the dynasty.
30 July 1793: Ali Burghul takes Tripoli (a usurper regime, drawn as a rebel state).
1794: a strip on the Tripolitanian frontier passes to Tunis.
19 January 1795: the Karamanli return to Tripoli and the usurper is crushed.
June 1805: the First Barbary War ends.

1811: Fezzan comes under direct rule from Tripoli, 'occupied in 1811/1812' on the Fezzan page (no occupier named); the Karamanli page has trans-Saharan expeditions in 1821 and Yusuf dropping his plan to conquer Bornu in 1824.

wars.name: Tripolitanian civil war
wars.outcome: Karamanli victory: Hamet and Yusuf returned to Tripoli on 19 January 1795 with the aid of the Bey of Tunis and the rebels; Burghul fled to Egypt.

wars.name: First Barbary War
wars.outcome: Peace of 10 June 1805 (infobox: 4 June); $60,000 for the American prisoners; no territorial change recorded.

wars.name: Karamanli civil war and Ottoman return
wars.outcome: Yusuf abdicated in 1832 for his son Ali II; 'civil war soon resulted' and Mahmud II's troops deposed Ali II in 1835 and reestablished direct control.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages: the coastal frontier with Tunis was not fixed until 1886 (Libya-Tunisia border page, read for the ottoman-tripolitania dossier) and the Saharan, Fezzan and Cyrenaican limits are tribal.
